reviews.summary: The live today.json and stats.json agree on the 2026-11-04 date and the 05:20:33Z scan time. The code derives dates from the scan time, and a no-scan build adds no history row and moves no date.

The live home page shows 'Latest published scan: 2026-11-04 05:20 UTC', matching stats.json generated. The 04:00 UTC start is a separate sentence with no promised duration, and the Added today heading names 'scan of 2026-11-04 UTC'. The page has no form, only the ld+json script, and the footer is kept.

The Rust and Python cards show exact paths and dated per-language share lines matching the home table and stats.json date. index.json keys are intact, stats.json generated is unchanged, and the footer, no-form and no-script constraints hold.

The home page uses a fixed minimum 5 pp sparkline span, so the 0.1 pp AGENTS.md move is 0.8 px on a 48 px chart. The baseline label (3 days) matches stats.json history, and the cite line names the scan date and points to history[].

Repo cards show the first-seen line for present files, with the first-scan note on rust-lang/rust and 2026-11-04 on nats-io/nats-server. index.json additions are optional keys only, and stats.json 'generated' is unchanged.

The live stats.json and llms.txt meet every acceptance criterion and negative case I could check. The history rows have shares, history_days is 3, change_7d_pp is null, and llms.txt labels the scan and build times separately and has the added/removed unit line.
